plan: This auction structure (pay second-highest sealed bid if you win) is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. My value is $9, so I will bid exactly $9. This ensures I win only when profitable (value exceeds price paid) and never overpay.

This auction mechanic effectively functions as a second-price sealed-bid auction: I exit at my sealed bid, and if I win, I pay the second-highest bid. Bidding my true value ($9) is the dominant strategy—it ensures I win whenever profitable (value > price paid) and never overpay, since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid.

This auction mechanism functions as a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid amount, regardless of their own bid. In such mechanisms, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks winning at a loss. Since my value is $34, I should bid exactly $34 to ensure optimal outcomes in all scenarios.
